_doc: #564 THE ONE MAP from an app's REAL installer (PackageManager.getInstallSourceInfo().installingPackageName) to the Store ▸ Phone Apps origin button. Read by PhoneAppActions; nothing else in the store names an installer package. Foreign store -> the button opens that store's own page for the app ({pkg} is substituted, and the intent is aimed at the installer so market:// lands in the store that installed it, not whichever handler wins). `ours` is a Cloud fleet member (by the fleet manifest, or installed by this app) -> the host's Store ▸ Cloud page, where we update it. `unknown` is anything else (sideloaded APK, adb, no installer recorded) -> the system App info screen. Adding a store = one entry under `sources`.

resolver._doc: #571 WE ARE THE STORE. Per EXTERNAL app, the ORDERED install sources this store tries on a phone that has no other store: `vendor` = the vendor's own official direct-APK endpoint; `fdroid` = the official F-Droid repo (index-v1.jar, JAR-signed by the pinned `cert_sha256`, per-version sha256 in the index); `play` = the Google Play deep-link — Play publishes NO APK URL, so the deep-link IS the official Play path and the row carries a visible 'needs Play' badge. Read by SourceResolver through PhoneAppActions.sources; `order` is the only legal ranking and an app's `sources` must be a subsequence of it. A `play` source carries NOTHING but its kind: a URL on it would be a fake. An app absent from `apps` still resolves — to the Play deep-link alone — so every package the vault or an import names has a row. Fleet (Cloud) apps are NOT here: they install through the constellation manifest and the updater's release path, one downloader for the fleet. VENDOR FIELDS: `apk` = URL template ({version} from the feed, {asset} from `abis`); `abis` = ABI -> asset fragment, chosen by AbiUpdateTag over Build.SUPPORTED_ABIS; `feed` = official JSON version endpoint, `version_name`/`version_code`/`apk_key`/`sha256_key` = dot paths into it; `version_re` = one-group regex normalising the feed's version string; `sha256` = URL of a sidecar whose body is a bare hex or the sha256sum(1) form. A vendor source with no feed has no version probe: it re-fetches whatever the vendor serves today and the updater's downgrade guard decides. EVIDENCE 2026-09-25 from this container: every `feed`, `apk` and `sha256` below answered 200 with the declared shape; F-Droid's api answered 404 for telegram/bitwarden/firefox/brave/obsidian/signal/whatsapp, which is why they carry no `fdroid` source; download.mozilla.org's fennec-latest redirector serves Firefox 68 (2020) and is deliberately NOT declared.
